exposure: Post-placental intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) insertion during lower segment caesarean section (LSCS)
outcome: Maternal complications (expulsion, displaced IUCD, perforation, hemorrhage, sepsis, menorrhagia, persistent pelvic pain)
cohort: 100 patients undergoing lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) who received a post-placental IUCD insertion, excluding those with conditions like anemia, major degree placenta previa, cardiac diseases, uncontrolled GDM, fibroid uterus, chorioamnionitis, or unwilling for the method.
finding: Post-placental IUCD insertion during LSCS was found to be a safe contraceptive procedure, with menorrhagia in 3 patients and persistent pelvic pain in one, but no expulsions, perforations, or sepsis observed.
mod_finding: The study found that post-placental IUCD insertion during lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) is a safe procedure with minimal complications for women who deliver by this mode.
